row1.revenue: Amazon leads the revenue race with $716.9 B, outpacing Walmart by a slim $3.7 B margin; the gap between the top two is relatively narrow compared to the $238.1 B difference between Amazon and Apple.

row1.total_liabilities: JPMorgan Chase leads with $4.1 trillion in total liabilities, far ahead of Bank of America’s $3.1 trillion and a steep gap to the tech giants, whose liabilities top out at Amazon’s $407 billion. row1.cash_and_equivalents: JPMorgan Chase leads with $343.3 B in cash and equivalents, outpacing Bank of America’s $239.3 B by $104 B and Amazon’s $86.8 B by $256.5 B. The gap between the top two banks is the largest, highlighting their stronger liquidity positions.
row1.gross_profit: Amazon (AMZN) tops the list with a gross profit of $360.5 B, outpacing Alphabet (GOOGL) by $120.2 B and leading the field by a wide margin. The next three firms-Apple, Microsoft, and Walmart-cluster around $230 B to $178 B, showing a tighter but still significant gap to Amazon.
row1.operating_income_ebit: Apple leads with an operating income of $158.1B, outpacing Microsoft by $2.9B and NVIDIA by $27.7B, highlighting a clear top‑tier advantage in EBIT among the group.
